headline: Postprandial Walking is Better for Lowering the Glycemic Effect of Dinner than Pre-Dinner Exercise in Type 2 Diabetic Individuals
implication: For a dinner-centered type 2 diabetes use case, post-meal walking appears more targeted than pre-meal walking, but the study does not prove a whole-day or every-meal benefit.
caveat: Small acute study; dinner-only exposure; type 2 diabetes population; no repeated every-meal intervention; total 4-hour AUC was not significantly different.

headline: Three 15-min Bouts of Moderate Postmeal Walking Significantly Improves 24-h Glycemic Control in Older People at Risk for Impaired Glucose Tolerance
implication: Three 15-minute walks after meals improved 24-hour glycemic control and were especially useful after dinner compared with a sustained morning or afternoon walk.
caveat: Very small sample; older high-risk adults rather than broad adult population; tightly controlled calorimeter setting; short acute exposure.

headline: Advice to walk after meals is more effective for lowering postprandial glycaemia in type 2 diabetes mellitus than advice that does not specify timing: a randomised crossover study
implication: In type 2 diabetes, specifying 10-minute walks after each main meal lowered postprandial glycemia more than generic daily walking advice with the same nominal activity target.
caveat: Short intervention periods; advice-based free-living exposure; adults with type 2 diabetes rather than general adults; unblinded behavior change study.

headline: Impact of post-meal and one-time daily exercise in patient with type 2 diabetes mellitus: a randomized crossover study
implication: For type 2 diabetes, 15 minutes of brisk walking after each meal may outperform concentrating the same total walking time into one morning bout.
caveat: No CGM; no carbohydrate counting; no clear washout; telephonic reminders and wristband monitoring; clinical T2D sample may not generalize to healthy adults.

headline: A comparison of acute glycaemic responses to accumulated or single bout walking exercise in apparently healthy, insufficiently active adults
implication: Three 10-minute walks after meals and one 30-minute after-dinner walk both lowered dinner glucose compared with no exercise; they were not different from each other for the dinner response.
caveat: Small sample; apparently healthy insufficiently active adults; acute design; primary reported difference concentrated after dinner.

headline: Effect of postprandial moderate-intensity walking for 15-min on glucose homeostasis in type 2 diabetes mellitus patients
implication: Fifteen-minute moderate walks after each meal reduced CGM-derived 24-hour glycemic exposure and variability compared with the no-exercise day, but the small fixed-sequence design limits certainty.
caveat: N=11; fixed order in the extracted record; acute inpatient two-day comparison; mixed diabetes medications; limited safety details accessible in extraction.

headline: Two bouts of exercise before meals, but not after meals, lower fasting blood glucose

caveat: Dose and timing evidence varies by population, meal, comparator, and endpoint; keep implementation claims practical and bounded.

headline: Slow postmeal walking reduces postprandial glycemia in middle-aged women

caveat: Small sample; healthy women only; carbohydrate-rich meal; acute exposure rather than repeated daily protocol; publisher PDF likely paywalled.

headline: Slow Post Meal Walking Reduces the Blood Glucose Response: An Exploratory Study in Female Pakistani Immigrants
